title: Play
description: A football play. References a formation by id (the formation file in data/formations/) and adds per-player assignments, motions, reads, success/failure analysis, and tags.

aliases.description: Alternate names this play is known by (different terminology trees).

formation.description: ID of the formation this play uses (matches a file in data/formations/). Player labels in assignments must match labels in the referenced formation.

rpo_type.description: For play_type 'rpo' only — which RPO read mechanic the play uses. 'alert' = a pre-snap decision off the defense's alignment (the called run is checked to a quick pass). 'peek' = a post-snap read of a conflict linebacker while riding the HB mesh — give, or pull and throw. 'read' = a post-snap read where the QB is himself a run threat (zone-read / QB-run RPO), reading a specific edge or second-level defender. Optional; meaningful only when play_type is 'rpo'.

ball_carrier.description: Label of the player who has the ball at the end of the play (e.g. 'HB' for a run, 'QB' for a designed scramble, the receiver who is the primary read for a pass).

primary_read.description: Label of the primary receiver (pass plays).

checkdown.description: Label of the safety-valve receiver if all reads are covered.

run_reads.description: Ball-carrier read progression for run plays. Each entry names what the runner reads at that priority and where to go based on the result. Analogous to a QB's read tree but for the ground game.

priority.description: 1 = first read, 2 = second read, 3 = third read, etc.

read_key.description: What the ball carrier reads — a defender, blocker, or landmark. E.g. 'backside DE', 'playside linebacker', 'pulling guard', 'C-gap', 'frontside A-gap'.

run_to.description: Where to go if this read is available / the gap opens. E.g. 'cut outside', 'bang the A-gap', 'follow the puller through the C-gap', 'cut back behind the center'.

notes.description: Optional coaching point or concept note for this read.

motions.description: Pre-snap (or at-snap) motions. Each motion is tagged mandatory or optional.

assignments.description: Per-player assignment. Should cover all 11 players in the referenced formation.

strengths.description: What this play does well — situations and matchups it's built for.

weaknesses.description: Where this play struggles — defensive reactions or matchups it can't beat.

best_vs_defense.description: Defensive coverages or fronts this play attacks well (e.g. 'cover-2', 'over-front', 'cover-3').

defensive_counters.description: Pre-snap defensive ALIGNMENTS that beat or threaten this play. Each entry is a look the QB can recognize before the snap by scanning the defense — NOT a post-snap movement. The QB sees the alignment, then checks to an audible (the playbook's counter_responses map each counter_id to an audible). Post-snap adjustments are handled by the play's run_reads / primary_read progression and assignment alt_paths, not here. Distinct from 'weaknesses' (static play shortcomings) and 'worst_vs_defense' (season-long matchup problems). Each entry has a stable counter_id so playbooks can reference it from their counter_responses field.

counter_id.description: Stable kebab-case id unique within this play (e.g. 'pinch-dl', 'loaded-box'). A stable handle that playbook counter_responses reference — it need not perfectly describe the alignment, and should NOT be changed once playbooks reference it.

pre_snap_look.description: The defensive ALIGNMENT the QB sees pre-snap. Must be observable before the snap — a static picture, not a post-snap movement. E.g. 'Both DTs in tight 3-techniques shaded inside the guards', '8 defenders inside the tackle box with a single-high safety', 'Both corners pressed at the line on the outside WRs'.

qb_key.description: The single fastest visual recognition cue — what the QB scans to identify this look in one glance. E.g. 'Count the box', 'Check the safety shell — one high', 'Scan the interior DL shade'.

read_category.description: Which part of the defense the QB scans to identify this counter. 'box-count' = number of defenders inside the tackle box. 'safety-shell' = number and depth of deep safeties (0/1/2-high). 'dl-alignment' = defensive-line technique and shade. 'lb-depth' = linebacker depth and width (walked up, stacked, cheated). 'cb-leverage' = cornerback depth and leverage (press/off, inside/outside).

why.description: One sentence on WHY this alignment beats or threatens the play. Helps a coach understand the mechanism (e.g. 'Inside-shaded tackles kill the down-block angles; the off-tackle hole is dead before the pull arrives').

typical_against.description: Defensive fronts/coverages where you'd commonly see this alignment (e.g. ['over-front', '4-3 base']). Optional.

flip_reads.description: Pre-snap alignment reads that tell the QB to FLIP this play's direction — same as defensive_counters in form (a look the QB scans before the snap), but the response is to mirror rather than audible to a different play. 'mirror-play' = run this exact play flipped to the other side (call the play's -left/-right mirror). 'mirror-formation' = flip the whole formation to its mirror, re-setting the defense's strength call, then run the play. Used for the 'check-with-me' run-direction decision and the formation-flip decision.

flip_id.description: Stable kebab-case id unique within this play (e.g. 'overshift-strong', 'box-heavy-callside').

pre_snap_look.description: The defensive ALIGNMENT the QB sees pre-snap that triggers the flip — a static picture, observable before the snap (e.g. 'Front overshifted to the called side — an extra hat in the strong-side box').

qb_key.description: The single fastest visual cue the QB scans to identify this look (e.g. 'Count the box by side — called side is +1').

read_category.description: Which part of the defense the QB scans — same enum as defensive_counters.read_category.

flip_to.description: 'mirror-play' = run this play flipped to the other side (its mirror play). 'mirror-formation' = flip the entire formation to its mirror, then run the play.

why.description: One sentence on why flipping beats the look (e.g. 'Running into the overshift is into the teeth; flipping attacks the lighter box').

typical_against.description: Defensive fronts/coverages where you'd commonly see this alignment. Optional.

common_uses.description: Game situations where you'd typically call this play.

run_concept_ref.description: Foreign key into data/concepts/run-concepts/ (kebab-case id). Set for run and play-action plays.

pass_concept_ref.description: Foreign key into data/concepts/pass-concepts/ (kebab-case id). Set for pass and play-action plays.

pass_protection_ref.description: Foreign key into data/concepts/pass-protections/ (kebab-case id). Set for pass, play-action, and screen plays.

concepts.description: Multi-concept composition (the Erhardt-Perkins model — a play is a package of concepts, callable from many formations). A play can run several concepts at once, each occupying a subset of the formation: e.g. Smash on the left two receivers + Spacing on the right three + a QB-run concept. Each entry foreign-keys into data/concepts/pass-concepts/ or run-concepts/ and names the players that execute it. A play uses EITHER the single-valued run_concept_ref / pass_concept_ref (a single-concept play) OR this array (a multi-concept play) — not both.

concept_ref.description: Foreign key into data/concepts/pass-concepts/ (when concept_type is 'pass') or data/concepts/run-concepts/ (when 'run').

concept_type.description: Which concept library this entry references.

players.description: Player labels (matching the play's formation) that execute this concept. A concept may occupy as few as one player (a QB-run) or span the whole formation (four-verticals).

field_area.description: Optional shorthand for where the concept sits in the formation.

is_primary.description: True for the concept the QB works first post-snap. Exactly one concept entry in a play should be marked primary.

philosophy_ref.description: Foreign key into data/concepts/philosophies/ (kebab-case id). Prefer this over the freeform 'philosophy' string for validated links.

era.description: Era when this play was/is most associated with (e.g. '1990s NFL', 'modern Air Raid').

famous_examples.description: Coaches, teams, or notable instances of this play.

tags.description: Free-form tags. Conventionally includes a level tag (high-school, college, nfl, any-level), philosophy/concept tags (power-run, air-raid, west-coast, spread, gap-scheme), and situation tags (red-zone, short-yardage, hurry-up).

verified_in_games.description: List of game_ids where this play has been manually verified in-game (recreated in the editor and confirmed to work as designed). Each entry must match a profile in data/games/.

player.description: Player label from the referenced formation (e.g. 'Z', 'HB', 'SLOT').

type.description: Mandatory: the play assumes the motion happened — running it without motion changes the concept. Optional: motion is a check the QB / coach can call (e.g. for matchup leverage), but the play works without it.

end_position.description: Where the motioning player ends up at snap (universal coords). Optional — start position comes from the formation.

snap_on_motion.description: True if the ball is snapped while the player is still in motion (e.g. jet motion). False / omitted means the player is set before snap.

role.description: What the player does on this play. 'handoff' is for the QB on a designed run.

depth_yd.description: Route break depth in yards (for routes), or push depth for blockers.

blocking_scheme.description: Blocking scheme when role is a block variant (e.g. 'down-block', 'kickout', 'pull-around', 'reach', 'man-protection', 'invite-rusher').

is_primary.description: True if this player is the primary read (for routes) or the primary ball-carrier.

path.description: Polyline waypoints in yards (universal coords) relative to the player's start position. The PRIMARY path. Color depends on role (orange for ball_carrier, magenta for FB lead, green for pulling lineman, light gray for pass-block, etc.).

priority.description: Read priority — drawn in matching color (primary=orange, secondary=blue, tertiary=lavender, checkdown=light gray).

alt_paths.description: Additional path alternatives for the same player. Used to show HB read options on a run play (e.g. BANG/BEND/BOUNCE on stretch zone) — the primary `path` is the first read, alt_paths add the secondary and tertiary options.

beats_coverage.description: Override for which coverage type this assignment is designed to attack. If absent, falls back to the route's default beats_coverage (when role=route).
